title: [Perf][MoE] Hopper MegaMoE: run block-FP8 MoE on FlashInfer's SM90 megakernel
body:
## Overview

vLLM has no MegaMoE that runs on Hopper today:

- the DeepGEMM MegaMoE (`deep_gemm_mega_moe`) requires SM100;
- the FlashInfer MoE-EP megakernels (`flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl`, `flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm`) require SM100

This PR runs block-FP8 MoE checkpoints on Hopper with FlashInfer's SM90 FP8 MegaMoE, which ships in FlashInfer 0.7.2. The kernel fuses dispatch, both expert GEMMs and combine. It goes through the existing `--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` path with no model code, so any block-FP8 MoE can use it.

Related:
- #58540: the same kernel, but for DeepSeek-V4 FP4 checkpoints converted to FP8, and on files that #54049 removed.
- #62073: Beam on SM100. It contains the same idle-rank change as this PR.
- #60895: DeepGEMM MegaMoE for GLM-5.3-Flash, SM100 only.
- #53527: DeepSeek-V4 through a DeepGEMM fork.

## Claims

- GLM-5.3-Flash on 8x H200 (DP8/EP8, 128K/512 decode, MTP3): +11% to +18% output throughput and -6% to -14% TPOT p50, at concurrency 8 to 192.
- One MoE layer at EP8: -7% at 8 tokens/rank, up to -48% at 8192 tokens/rank.
- GSM8K: 0.919 vs 0.917.
- The backend is opt-in. Default backends do not change.

## Validation

**Decode.**
- Hardware and model: 8x H200, GLM-5.3-Flash FP8.
- Baseline: the default FP8 path, FlashInfer CUTLASS with allgather/reducescatter. All other settings are vLLM defaults.
- Load: DecodeBenchConnector, ISL 128K / OSL 512, MTP3 with synthetic acceptance [0.8, 0.6, 0.5], N = 2C prompts.
- Runs: A/B/A with two passes per arm. "Base" is the mean of the two baseline arms.

| C | 8 | 32 | 64 | 128 | 192 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| output tok/s, base | 911 | 2895 | 5204 | 7977 | 10074 |
| output tok/s, this PR | 1009 (+10.8%) | 3402 (+17.5%) | 5893 (+13.2%) | 9326 (+16.9%) | 11917 (+18.3%) |
| TPOT p50 ms, base → this PR | 7.60 → 6.86 | 9.20 → 7.96 | 9.27 → 8.72 | 10.81 → 9.85 | 11.58 → 10.87 |

**MoE layer, EP8.** GLM-5.3-Flash expert shapes, milliseconds per layer:

| tokens/rank | 8 | 64 | 128 | 512 | 1024 | 8192 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| baseline | 0.265 | 0.381 | 0.446 | 0.834 | 1.378 | 9.204 |
| this PR | 0.247 | 0.294 | 0.310 | 0.461 | 0.754 | 4.798 |

**GSM8K.** 1319 questions, 5-shot, natural MTP3: 0.917 → 0.919.

**Tests.**

```bash
pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_fi_moe_ep.py tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py
# CPU: 29 passed. SM90 GPU: 8 passed (4 expert shapes x EP2/EP4).
```

The SM90 GPU tests need at least two Hopper GPUs and `nvshmem4py`, so CI does not run them.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
vllm serve <GLM-5.3-Flash FP8> --data-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-num-seqs 64 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"DecodeBenchConnector","kv_role":"kv_both"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3,"rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_rates":[0.8,0.6,0.5]}' \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl   # omitted for the baseline

vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 131072 --random-output-len 512 \
  --ignore-eos --request-rate inf --max-concurrency $C --num-prompts $((2 * C))
```
</details>

## Details

- **Kernel.**
  - FlashInfer `Sm90PullFp8MegaMoeConfig`, with FP32 128x128 weight scales and a SwiGLU clamp.
  - FlashInfer's push-style SM90 backend has no SwiGLU clamp, so it cannot serve `swiglu_limit` models.
- **Weights.**
  - The kernel wants FC1 rows interleaved as `[pair, {gate, up}, 8]` under one 128x128 scale. Each scale block therefore covers rows from two checkpoint blocks, and both use `max(s_gate, s_up)`.
  - This is exact for power-of-two scales, which GLM-5.3-Flash has. Other checkpoints get one extra E4M3 rounding on half of the FC1 rows.
- **Workspaces.**
  - The kernel always processes its whole token buffer, with a launch geometry picked for that size. With a single buffer sized at `max_num_batched_tokens`, decode is slower than the baseline.
  - The adapter therefore adds 64-, 256- and 1024-token workspaces. Each call uses the smallest one that fits the largest batch across DP ranks.
- **Loaders.**
  - The fp8, compressed-tensors, online FP8 and Quark FP8 MoE methods now call the experts' `process_weights_after_loading`. It is a no-op for other experts.
  - The SM90 path is chosen from the quant config, not the weight dtype. FP8 weights keep their dtype, so a rebuild from preprocessed weights picks the same path.
- **Idle ranks.** With pass-through stages, the experts own the EP collective. A rank without tokens therefore still enters them. The change is identical to the one in #62073.
- **Limitations.**
  - The backend needs expert parallelism and `nvshmem4py`.
  - It rejects DBO, runtime weight transfer and `apply_router_weight_on_input`.
  - Shared experts are not fused.
  - FlashInfer's SM90 input staging is torch-composed, about 1.2 ms per step at C128.

title: [Perf][Attention] Remove D2H sync from FlashInfer SM90 sparse MLA plan under async scheduling
body:
## Purpose

With async scheduling, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` did a blocking D2H copy on every metadata build. FlashInfer bakes each row's `kv_len` into its schedule on the host, and `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound` is optimistic under async spec decode, so the builder copied `positions` / `seq_lens` back to get exact lengths. With MTP that happens on every draft step too. On GLM-5.3-Flash this made async scheduling *slower* than `--no-async-scheduling` (11.1 vs 7.7 ms TPOT at c=1).

How it works:

1. **Plan on the CPU with the upper bound plus slack.** The host bound, padded by 32 tokens and capped at the max valid count, is available without touching the GPU, so there's no sync.
2. **Clamp on the GPU.** FlashInfer keeps the plan in its int workspace as a list of work items with `kv_start`/`kv_end`. A small Triton kernel (`_clamp_work_kv_end`) computes each row's exact valid count on device from `seq_lens` / `query_start_loc` / `req_id_per_token` (same formula as before) and clamps every work item's `kv_end` to it. The FA3 kernel never reads past `kv_end`, so the slack (and the `-1` tail of the index buffer) is never touched.
3. **Reuse the plan across steps.** Contexts grow by a few tokens per step and the slack absorbs that, so while the new bounds still fit, `wrapper.plan()` is skipped and only the clamp runs. This is also why no-async gets slightly faster.

```
before:  GPU seq_lens --(blocking D2H)--> CPU exact lens --> plan --> run
after:   CPU upper bound + 32 --> plan (usually reused)
         GPU: clamp kv_end to exact lens (Triton, no sync) --> run
```

Notes:
- This reads `wrapper._plan_info` and the planned int workspace (the `MLAPlanInfo` layout from `scheduler.cuh`). The plan-info length is asserted, and the per-work capacity is read from the layout rather than hardcoded.
- With adaptive verification the host query split may not match the device one, so the host bound falls back to the batch max for every row.
- The exact (syncing) path is only used when there's no host upper bound.
- Only affects `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` (Hopper; the default sparse backend for NoPE models such as GLM-5.3-Flash).

**Not a duplicate:** I searched open PRs touching this backend. #55222 fixes the fp8 plan dtype and indexer workspace sizing, and #58260 chunks plan/run for >16k-row steps. Neither addresses the sync. #58260 does touch `plan()` / `build()`, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase; I'm happy to do it.

## Test Plan

- Unit tests: `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py` on H100. I updated the existing tests to the new `plan()` signature and added two GPU tests against real FlashInfer. One checks that an upper-bound plan plus the device clamp matches an exact plan (including MTP-style multi-query rows around `index_topk` and a batch spanning several clamp blocks). The other checks that the plan is reused across growing contexts without replanning.
- E2E: `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, TP8 on H100, fp8 KV cache, MTP with 5 speculative tokens, `max-model-len 32768`. Benchmark: `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 128 --ignore-eos` at concurrency 1/8/32, at least 32 prompts, each point run twice, no profiler.
- Accuracy: `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` (1319 questions, 5-shot).
- Syncs: a torch profiler trace on the patched server shows no blocking sync left in the draft-step metadata build (before: 13 per ~5 steps, ~79 ms total, at `_kv_lens_host`).

All E2E runs, baseline included, have the fp8 plan-dtype fix from #55222 applied locally, since fp8 KV on this backend fails without it.

## Test Result

Unit tests: 18 passed.

Mean TTFT / median TTFT / mean TPOT (ms), average of 2 runs:

| | c=1 | c=8 | c=32 |
|---|---|---|---|
| main, async | 136.6 / 138.8 / 11.09 | 226.2 / 188.6 / 21.87 | 338.2 / 319.9 / 45.04 |
| **this PR, async** | 128.1 / 126.9 / **6.86** | 188.0 / 152.7 / **17.36** | 283.7 / 251.5 / **37.04** |
| main, no-async | 129.8 / 128.8 / 7.70 | 189.2 / 157.8 / 18.20 | 258.9 / 175.5 / 42.71 |
| this PR, no-async | 124.2 / 123.8 / 7.47 | 177.2 / 152.0 / 17.95 | 254.7 / 170.6 / 41.72 |

With async scheduling, TPOT drops 38% / 21% / 18%, and async is now faster than no-async at every concurrency.

GSM8K is unchanged: 0.913 → 0.921 (async), 0.911 → 0.917 (no-async). MTP mean acceptance length stays ~4.2. The random-token bench has ~no draft acceptance, so its TPOT is close to the worst case for spec decode.

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Pin host tensors passed to the FlashInfer SM90 sparse MLA plan
body:
## Overview

`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` passes pageable CPU tensors (qo/kv indptr, KV lengths) to `BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper.plan()`. The wrapper copies them to the GPU with `non_blocking=True`, so `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` rejects the copy as an implicit sync. On GLM-5.3-Flash on H200 the engine dies on its first request. This PR stages the tensors in pinned memory, the same pattern #54660 applied to the FlashInfer backend.

## Claims

- GLM-5.3-Flash (H200, SM90 sparse MLA) now runs under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. Before this change it failed on the first request.
- Every host tensor `plan()` copies to the device is now pinned. The reused staging buffers stay unpinned, as in `flashinfer.py`.
- No performance claim: DEP8 decode throughput is neutral within run-to-run noise (table below).

## Validation

**Reproducer** (GLM-5.3-Flash, TP4 + MTP3, 4×H200):

    VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
      --tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-num-seqs 64 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
      --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0}' \
      --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
    vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
      --dataset-name speed_bench --speed-bench-dataset-subset throughput_1k \
      --speed-bench-output-len 256 --num-prompts 64 --max-concurrency 16

| | implicit-sync errors | requests completed |
|---|---|---|
| main | 17. The engine died: `Tensor.copy_: a non_blocking H2D copy that may be silently synchronous (the CPU tensor is not pinned)`, raised from FlashInfer `_stage_metadata` under `_SM90State._plan` | 0 / 64 |
| this PR | 0 | 64 / 64 |

**Unit tests** (H200): `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py`: 25 passed. `test_plan_uses_state_params` now asserts that the tensors handed to the wrapper are pinned whenever pinned memory is available.

**Performance** (DEP8 decode-only, 8×H200, DecodeBenchConnector, ISL 128K / OSL 512, MTP3 with synthetic acceptance [0.8, 0.6, 0.5], warm pass). C=128 was measured twice; the other points once.

| C | main tok/s, TPOT ms | this PR tok/s, TPOT ms |
|---|---|---|
| 64 | 3534, 12.89 | 3927, 11.45 |
| 128 | 4867, 17.48 | 5137, 17.04 |
| 192 | 5684, 20.53 | 5641, 20.29 |

## Details

`_SM90State._plan` fills reusable CPU buffers (`_qo_cpu`, `_kv_cpu`, `_lens_cpu`) in place and passes them to the wrapper. With `use_cuda_graph=True`, the wrapper's `_stage_metadata` copies them into its reserved device buffers with `non_blocking=True`. From pageable memory CUDA may synchronize to stage that copy, which is what the sync check flags.

The fix passes a `.pin_memory()` copy of each buffer instead of making the buffers themselves pinned. PyTorch's caching host allocator keeps a pinned block alive until the async copy that reads it completes, so the next plan cannot overwrite in-flight data. Pinning the reused buffers directly would need explicit events to avoid that race. This mirrors `vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py` since #54660.

Not a duplicate: no open PR touches this backend's plan staging. #58684 removed this plan's D2H sync; this change covers the H2D side.

Out of scope: `plan()` itself costs 4–6.5 ms per call, measured without the profiler. Most of that is FlashInfer's Python workload validation (`_fa_plan_work_count`), which runs over all `max_num_batched_tokens` rows, twice per plan. That belongs in a FlashInfer change.
